title: AI apps recognize Hebrew and X requests
lines: The tool descriptions and server instructions for AI apps now include Hebrew and X (Twitter) trigger words.
The publish tool says it posts nothing to X.

title: Four ready-made prompts for AI apps
lines: AI apps get four slash commands: make a thread from notes, tighten a draft, review before publishing, and rewrite a hook.
Each has an English and a Hebrew description.

title: AI apps can load a thread-drafts skill
lines: The server now offers one skill about X thread drafts, with English and Hebrew trigger text.

title: MCP plan closed out in the docs
lines: The plan tracker marks the AI app tasks done.
The feature docs describe the four slash commands, the skill and the Hebrew and X wording.

title: Drafts are readable only by their owner
lines: Opening a draft that belongs to someone else now shows Draft not found.
Opening or exporting a draft without signing in is refused.
The editor shows a sign-in prompt when you are signed out, and never shows a cached copy.
The Share button is hidden until share links get an expiry.

title: Share links expire and can be revoked
lines: Share links stop working after a set time. The default is 1 hour, and you can choose 60 seconds up to 7 days.
You can revoke one share link, or all links of a draft.
The new Share menu copies a reusable link that lasts 15 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day or 7 days.
Links from the X Thread and Agent link buttons are still single-use, and now expire after 1 hour.
Existing unused links now expire 1 hour after they were made.

title: Plan for faster MCP and API requests
lines: A new plan lists the speed tasks, based on measurements.
The agent rules now say product code must not grow unless the pull request names its task.

title: Every API request reports its timing
lines: Each API response now carries a timing header with total time, database time, number of queries and whether the start was cold.
Each request also writes one log line with the route, status, timings and region.
The smoke test prints timing and compression lines but never fails on them.

title: Export is a menu button next to Share
lines: Export is now a button with a menu, next to Share, on phones and desktop.
The Share menu on phones opens above the bottom bar. It used to be off screen.

title: Plans for admin tools and the bottom bar
lines: Two new plans cover the admin tools and the phone bottom bar.
The share-links plan has a new task order and an adjusted sign-out task.

title: One slim bar on every signed-in page
lines: The draft list, the editor and the API tokens page share one slim bar. On phones it sits at the bottom, one row, 44 pixels high.
Sign out is a small icon button in the bar. You can hide the bar, and your choice is kept in this browser.
Icons replace the emoji on Share, Agent link, X Thread and Export.
The bar no longer covers the last post on phones.

title: A copy link on the app approval page
lines: The approval page for connecting an app greets you by your GitHub username and shows a link with a Copy link button, to open the request in another browser.
When you are signed out, the same link opens a Sign in to continue page, with the same Copy link field, instead of sending you to GitHub.
These pages run one script, and no other.

title: Sign out now ends the server session
lines: Sign out now ends your browser session on the server, not only the cookie. Everyone signs in once more after this change.
Sign out also removes the drafts cached in this browser.
The app approval page has a Not you? Sign out link that returns to sign-in for the same request.

title: Test time budget raised to 55 seconds
lines: The total time allowed for the test suite goes from 50 to 55 seconds, after a run with all tests green took slightly over 50 seconds.

title: AI apps and the API get draft summaries
lines: The draft list can return post counts instead of full post text. The AI app draft list does this by default.
A new outline shows each post's character count against the 280 limit and the first 40 characters.

title: The editor uses the full width on phones
lines: On phones the editor fills the screen width, with smaller padding around the header, composer and embedded cards.
Embedded tweets are limited to the screen width, so they no longer widen the page.

title: Plan for thread views inside AI apps
lines: A new plan covers thread and drafts views inside Claude and ChatGPT.
No code changed.

title: Edit tools in AI apps return short results
lines: After an edit, the post and draft tools in AI apps return the draft outline and version instead of the whole draft.
Only the get draft tool returns post text.
API responses stay as they were.

title: Character counts follow the X rules
lines: Counts and the save limit now follow X rules: a link counts as 23, an emoji as 2, and direction marks as 2.
This applies in the editor, the splitter, draft summaries and post edits from the API and AI apps.

title: Post limits are explained in the docs
lines: The docs now give the post limit as 4000 characters, or 280 as X counts them.
The emoji counting works on Safari 16 and older.

title: Final docs for private drafts and share links
lines: The docs now cover private drafts, share link expiry and revoking, draft summaries and outline, and sign out.
The production smoke test checks the signed-out approval page.
The private drafts plan is marked done.

title: AI apps save threads as drafts by default
lines: The server text now tells AI apps when to save a written thread as a draft.
No tool or input changed.

title: Dependency audit checks only production packages for now
lines: The dependency audit that must pass before a merge covers production packages only, because a development-only package has a known issue with no fix yet.
The full audit still runs on every change and only reports. It must pass again by 2026-12-17, once that package is patched.

title: Plan for the settings menu
lines: A new plan covers a left menu, version info, a redesigned API tokens page and a changelog page.
The plan lists the open questions for the owner, with the agent's default for each.

title: The server reports its version
lines: A public version address and the app version tool for AI apps now return the commit, the deploy time and the database schema version.
The server version now includes the commit.

title: A left menu on every signed-in page
lines: A menu button at the start of each page header opens a left menu with Drafts, Theme, API tokens and apps, and Sign out.
Theme and the API tokens button leave the draft list header.
The phone bottom bar keeps Sign out.

title: A version line and an About page
lines: The menu ends with a small version line, showing the commit and deploy time, that opens a new About page.
The About page shows this app's build and the server's version, with a Copy button.
A Reload button appears when a newer version is available.

title: The API tokens page has three cards
lines: The page now has three cards: your API tokens, Connect an AI app, and Connected apps.
A new token shows in a one-time box with one large Copy button.
The heading is now API tokens and apps. Behavior is the same.

title: Paste-in text so AI apps save drafts
lines: The AI app guide has English and Hebrew text to paste into an AI app, so it saves threads as drafts.
The public guide for AI tools links to it.

title: The changelog is available from the API
lines: Signed-in users can read the changelog from the API, in pages of up to 50 entries (20 by default).
The app version tool for AI apps also returns the 5 newest changes.
The app does not show the changelog yet.

title: A Changelog page in the menu
lines: The menu has a Changelog item. It shows the running version, then the changes grouped by day, 20 at a time.
The About page links to it with See what changed.

title: Paste-in text card on the tokens page
lines: The API tokens page has a card with the English and Hebrew text to paste into an AI app, each with a Copy button.
The card also says where to paste it.

title: A check that AI apps save drafts
lines: A new optional check asks a model to handle written threads and questions, and tests that it saves threads as drafts and does not save when only answering.
It does not run in the automatic checks, and it skips itself without an API key.

title: The database connection stays open longer
lines: An idle database connection now stays open for 60 seconds, up from 10, so repeated requests reuse it.
The server also waits for the connection to finish before it suspends.

title: Image tools load only on image routes
lines: Routes that do not handle images now start faster, because the image storage code loads on first use.
Start-up time of the API handler fell from 145 to 288 ms down to 86 to 105 ms on the same machine.
The address checks for remote images work as before.

title: Test time budget raised to 70 seconds
lines: The total time allowed for the automatic test run goes from 55 to 70 seconds, because the same passing suite took 46 to 62 seconds on the build machines.
Per-file limits and test checks stay as they were.

title: Draft updates use one database query
lines: Updating a draft now takes 1 database query instead of 4.
Adding a post takes 4 queries instead of 7, and moving or removing a post takes 4 instead of 7.
Answers, statuses and headers stay as they were.

title: Post updates use one database write
lines: Updating a post now writes in one statement instead of a 4-statement transaction.
The post update tool for AI apps takes 3 queries instead of 6.
Answers, statuses and headers stay as they were.

title: AI app tool calls need one query less
lines: The token check and the tool-call count for AI apps now run as one query.
Each tool call takes one query less.
A request without a token is still refused before its body is read.

title: Image cleanup checks run as one query
lines: Deciding whether an uploaded image is still in use now takes one database check, instead of reading every draft.
Removing a post or an image with the AI app tools, deleting a draft and publishing keep any file that another draft of the same user still uses.
